answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, so the one intervention that can restore availability is shifting writes off that region. Rollback is disallowed by the security-patch constraint, so memory_b1 is not actionable. Circuit breaking (b4) would fail writes and violates the no-lost-writes objective. Read-replica routing (b5) addressed report/dashboard load, not the transactional write path. Capacity (b3) helped when provisioned before a peak; it is unverified as a mid-peak cure for a single-region write stall and may not fix a regional fault. memory_b2 is the closest prior: failover recovered latency in minutes with a clean traffic shift. Archives for b2 and b3 should confirm write integrity during failover and whether mid-incident capacity ever worked. One-shot constraint argues against a tiny canary that would leave most settlement writes on the sick primary. Downstream settlement value is at daily peak, so write-loss and dual-write/split-brain risk is flagged; confidence stays moderate until the two archives return.
